title.en: Cantilever tip load and spatial bending

summary: Change a tip load and inspect the continuous beam bend while its clamped root stays fixed.
objective: Expose the authoritative model and its visible response: cantilever tip load and spatial bending.
applies_when: Prismatic slender Euler-Bernoulli beam with constant E,I, fixed root, transverse tip force and small deflection; static linear elastic response without self-weight.
intent_signals: Change a tip load and inspect the continuous beam bend while its clamped root stays fixed.
example_prompts: Build an inspectable demonstration of cantilever tip load and spatial bending with parameter controls and a reset.
negative_signals: Not large rotations, shear-flexible short beams, buckling, plasticity, dynamic response or certified structural design.
not_for: Not large rotations, shear-flexible short beams, buckling, plasticity, dynamic response or certified structural design.

principles: A load slider recalculates static equilibrium; tweening between equilibria is not vibration.
The centerline bend and section orientation must come from the same displacement field.
implementation: Own length L in m, E in Pa, second area moment I in m^4 and signed transverse tip force P in N. Fix +x from the clamp toward the tip and one transverse +y axis. P is signed along +y, and w is displacement along that same fixed +y axis for either load sign. Use w(x)=P*x*x*(3*L-x)/(6*E*I), slope=P*x*(2*L-x)/(2*E*I), and M(x)=E*I*w''(x)=P*(L-x) in this section-moment convention. Require finite L,E,I>0 and finite P.

Sample physical centerline positions and orient cross sections normal to its tangent; retain section dimensions. Show a fixed clamp, tip force and optional undeformed ghost. A displayed displacement magnifier must not modify computed strain or physical readouts.

Allow load reversal and E or I edits; recompute mesh, slope and tip displacement together. Declare a small-slope/deflection applicability criterion for the chosen example and label out-of-regime inputs. Reset restores load and display magnification.
observable_checks: Verify w(0)=0, slope(0)=0, M(L)=0 and w(L)=P*L^3/(3*E*I).
With L=1 m,E=200 GPa,I=1e-8 m^4,P=10 N, tip displacement is 1/600 m; doubling P doubles it, and P=0 restores the undeformed centerline.
Reverse P in the same fixed coordinates: w(x;-P)=-w(x;P), including the tip. The transverse axis and undeformed reference do not flip with the load.

known_limits: Not large rotations, shear-flexible short beams, buckling, plasticity, dynamic response or certified structural design.
Authored reusable guidance; no solver or rendered artifact has been tested for this record.
creative_affordances: Use a cutaway, restrained ghost reference or annotated section only when it clarifies the modeled relation; a planar diagram remains valid when depth adds no information.

claims.statement: For a clamped prismatic beam under a transverse tip force P, the linear beam solution is w(x)=P*x^2*(3L-x)/(6EI), slope=P*x*(2L-x)/(2EI) and bending moment P*(L-x); the tip displacement follows as P*L^3/(3EI).
claims.scope: Prismatic slender Euler-Bernoulli beam with constant E,I, fixed root, transverse tip force and small deflection; static linear elastic response without self-weight.
